quote: fragen unter welchen Umständen, es auch die Eigenschaft 5 hat.
english: [we] ask under what circumstances it also has property 5.
topic: Hilbert lists properties of systems of forms (closure under addition and subtraction, closure under integral rational functions, divisibility, finite basis), defines a 'full system of forms', and sets out a plan to prove which properties such systems have.

triage.modern_statement: This reading assumes the page numbers the properties as (1) closure under addition, (2) closure under subtraction, (3) closure under integral rational (polynomial) functions, (4) a divisibility property, and (5) a finite basis. The page summary does not say which property is number 5, so that assumption is not verified. Under it, the question is: let S be a set of forms in k[x_1,…,x_n] that is a subring closed under polynomial combinations and has a divisibility closure property, such as an invariant ring or a ring of the form L ∩ k[x_1,…,x_n] for a subfield L. Under what conditions is S finitely generated as a k-algebra? This is the question behind Hilbert's 14th problem.
triage.answered_by: Partly answered, if the identification is right. Zariski (1954) proved finite generation for the cases n = 1 and n = 2 (Zariski's version of the problem). Nagata (1959) gave a counterexample to the general conjecture: the invariant ring of a 13-dimensional commutative unipotent group acting on a polynomial ring in 32 variables is not finitely generated. Hilbert himself had already proved finite generation for invariants of the classical groups (1890/1893).

evidence.claim: Hilbert conjectured that such algebras (intersections of a subfield with a polynomial ring, including invariant rings) are always finitely generated. Zariski proved this for n = 1 and n = 2 in 1954, and Nagata found a counterexample in 1959.
Nagata's counterexample is the ring of invariants of a 13-dimensional commutative unipotent group acting on k[x_1..x_16, t_1..t_16]; this ring is not finitely generated.
Nagata's TIFR lectures set out the original fourteenth problem (is the invariant ring I^G finitely generated over K?), Zariski's generalization, and related versions.

triage.why: The page lists closure properties and finite basis for systems of forms and asks when a system 'also has property 5'. This matches the finite-generation question Hilbert later posed as Problem 14 in 1900. However, the numbering of the five properties is my inference and was not checked against the manuscript. If property 5 is actually something else, such as a Nullstellensatz or radical-type property, this identification fails. In that case the note would be too fragmentary to identify from the summary alone. The general question is settled: true for n ≤ 2 and for reductive groups, false in general. It remains an active area, including finite-generation questions for invariants of non-reductive groups, unipotent actions and locally nilpotent derivations, but these sources do not document that current activity.
